Package neqsim.process.processmodel

Class ProcessModel.BoundaryStreamError

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.processmodel.ProcessModel.BoundaryStreamError
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
Enclosing class:
ProcessModel
public static final class ProcessModel.BoundaryStreamError extends Object implements Serializable
Per-stream convergence diagnostics for a single boundary stream.

Recorded on every outer iteration so that a non-converged model can name the stream responsible for the reported maximum flow, temperature or pressure error instead of only reporting the magnitude.

Version:
1.0
Author:
Even Solbraa

    • getProducerLabel

      public String getProducerLabel()
      Producing unit of this boundary stream as "area::unit".

      Equipment that auto-names its outlets (splitters emit "Split Stream_0", "Split Stream_1", ...) produces identical stream names all over a large plant, so the stream name alone cannot identify the offender. This label names the unit that produced the stream.

      Returns:
      "area::unit", or an empty string when the producer is unknown

    • getQualifiedName

    • getAbsoluteFlowChange

      public double getAbsoluteFlowChange()
      Absolute change in flow rate between the two last outer iterations.

      A large relative error on a very small absolute change is numerical noise on a stagnant leg rather than a real process residual; use this value to tell the two apart.

      Returns:
      absolute flow change in kg/hr

    • getMaxError

      public double getMaxError()
      Largest of the flow, temperature and pressure relative errors.
      Returns:
      maximum relative error for this stream

    • isFlowCollapsedToZero

      public boolean isFlowCollapsedToZero()
      Whether the stream flow collapsed from a non-zero value to (numerically) zero between the two last outer iterations. This produces a relative flow error of exactly 1.0 and usually means an upstream unit stopped producing the stream rather than a slowly converging recycle.
      Returns:
      true when the flow dropped from non-zero to zero

    • isFlowStartedFromZero

      public boolean isFlowStartedFromZero()
      Whether the stream flow started from (numerically) zero and became non-zero between the two last outer iterations.
      Returns:
      true when the flow started up from zero
